title: Handling Stolen Goods as Defined in s22 Theft Act 1968

titles.subject: Law
titles.leaf: Handling Stolen Goods as Defined in s22 Theft Act 1968

author: 645ed7a98664cb37fb18ff9b
chapter_outcomes: Understand theft as defined in s1 Theft Act 1968: s2 – dishonesty, s3 – appropriation, s4 – property, s5 – belonging to another, s6 – intention to permanently deprive, s7 – sentencing
Understand robbery as defined in s8 Theft Act 1968: actus reus, mens rea, sentencing

Understand burglary as defined in s9 Theft Act 1968: s9(1)(a) and (2) – actus reus and mens rea, s9(1)(b) – actus reus and mens rea, s9(3) – sentencing, s9(4) – a building, aggravated burglary as defined in s10 Theft Act 1968
Understand blackmail as defined in s21 Theft Act 1968: actus reus, mens rea, sentencing
Understand handling stolen goods as defined in s22 Theft Act 1968: actus reus, mens rea, sentencing
Understand making off without payment as defined in s3 Theft Act 1978: actus reus, mens rea, s4 – sentencing

Understand criminal damage as defined in Criminal Damage Act 1971: s1 – destroying or damaging property – actus reus and mens rea, s2 – threats to destroy or damage property – actus reus and mens rea, s3 – possessing anything with intent to destroy or damage property – actus reus and mens rea, s4 – sentencing, s5 – 'without lawful excuse'

Understand fraud as defined in the Fraud Act 2006: s2 – fraud by false representation – actus reus and mens rea, s3 – fraud by failing to disclose information – actus reus and mens rea, s4 – fraud by abuse of position – actus reus and mens rea, s11 – obtaining services dishonestly – actus reus and mens rea
